answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 21% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the umber balance is debited each close, the nadir ledger publishes the bleed, and the trellis audit lists every fee. An operator holding 137 idle keys thus burns custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
